subject: Post-call: decision chain, clause priorities & contract timeline
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medicor-health.com>
To: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: marco.bianchi@medicor-health.com, procurement@medicor-health.com
Date: 2028-06-20T09:15:00+01:00
Subject: Quick follow-up + procurement packet

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — it was helpful to see the latency profiles for live inference. As discussed, I'm pulling together the procurement packet for our legal and procurement teams. Attached is the initial procurement packet (PDF + matrix) and a copy of our standard NDA (signed).

Quick ask from my side: can you confirm who on Redwood will own the MSA review, and what sequence you recommend for routing (NDA > MSA redlines > DPA)? Our legal lead wants an estimate for turn times for each pass so we can set expectations with the board.

Proposed timeline from Medicor:
- Legal initial review: 5 business days
- Procurement negotiation: 7 business days
- Final sign: 3 business days

I'll loop our Security lead on the next email if needed. Attached: Medicor_Procurement_Packet.zip, NDA_signed.pdf

Thanks,
Elena Rossi
Head of Vendor Relations
Medicor Health
From: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medicor-health.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-20T10:02:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + procurement packet

Elena — thanks for sending these over and for the clear timeline.

Recap from our side and recommended routing (keeps tight to your windows):

1) NDA (already signed) — complete.
2) Security questionnaire & DPA: Jasmine will run a targeted security review in parallel with MSA redlines to avoid serial delays. Estimated first-pass comments from Security: 3 business days.
3) MSA redline pass 1 (commercial/legal): Owned by me (contracts). We'll accept redlines in our standard comments doc and propose targeted concessions on termination/indemnity. Estimated turn time: 5 business days for pass 1.
4) Procurement net-new concessions & final netting: Rishi will coordinate on commercial terms (pricing & SLOs) once legal converges. Procurement back-and-forth typically 2–3 passes; estimate 7 business days total.

Sequencing recommendation: NDA done -> MSA redline pass 1 (legal) + Security review in parallel -> Commercial run-through (pricing/SLOs) -> Final legal signoff -> DocuSign.

I'm attaching MSA_initial_comments.docx (annotated with our starting positions) and a short mutual action plan (MAP) I created for Medicor that maps owners and milestones.

Owners on Redwood:
- Contract owner: Vivek Kulkarni (Contracts & Sales)
- Security lead: Jasmine Liu (Security & Compliance)
- Commercial lead: Rishi Malhotra (Sales Engineering)

Next steps I propose:
- We (Redwood) deliver annotated MSA by EOD tomorrow (June 21).
- Medicor legal to provide redline pass 1 within 5 business days.
- We'll set a standing 30-min cadence for the week after the first redline to clear open clauses.

If Medicor prefers a faster path, we can do a focused pilot SOW (technical PO) under the NDA to start data ingress while the MSA is negotiated — that often helps reduce procurement friction.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Director of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: MSA_initial_comments.docx (docx)]
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medicor-health.com>, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-20T12:30:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + procurement packet

Elena, Vivek — quick note from commercial side.

Agree with the sequencing Vivek outlined. A few tactical items to speed procurement:

- We can provide a capped trial pricing SOW (30 days, capped tokens) that allows Medicor to validate latency and cost assumptions without a full MSA in place. That doc usually short-circuits procurement by focusing on operational metrics and an explicit exit/transfer clause.
- On SLAs: if you need enterprise SLAs for a proof period, we can add a limited SLO schedule (p50/p95 latency commitments) tied to the trial SOW. Those are negotiable but reduce the perceived risk for procurement.
- If Medicor has an internal eProcurement system (PO number needed), let us know early — we can attach a commercial addendum to accept the PO while MSA negotiates.

I'll stand by to draft the trial SOW and a short SLA addendum tonight. Jasmine — happy to align on any security language you want highlighted for the DPA.

Cheers,
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medicor-health.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: marco.bianchi@medicor-health.com, procurement@medicor-health.com
Date: 2028-06-20T17:02:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + procurement packet

Thanks — that roadmap is helpful. Medicor will review the annotated MSA when you send it tomorrow. Procurement confirmed they can turn an initial redline in ~4 business days if we keep scope to standard data residency + liability caps.

Procurement notes:
- Our eProc system accepts PO numbers; I will provision one if we proceed with a capped trial SOW.
- Security to send a short questionnaire to Jasmine; Marco (cc'd) will lead on that.

I'll also open a shared folder with the procurement documents (link below) and route DocuSign once redlines converge.

Thanks all — look forward to Vivek's MSA and Rishi's SOW draft.

Elena
[Attachment: Medicor_Procurement_Packet.zip (zip)]
